record.limits_note: Koyeb's startup programme advertises 'up to $30k in credits', which is a separate application, not a signup grant.
record.reliability_note: scale-to-zero is silent from the caller's side, a request after an hour pays a cold start instead of an error; the pricing page carries the banner 'Koyeb is joining Mistral AI to Build The Future of AI Infrastructure', which puts the free tier's longevity in question
record.notes: The pricing FAQ read says the opposite, in a section titled 'Why does Koyeb require a credit card?'. This is the clearest instance of the complaint about undisclosed holds: USD 29, and a charge on top of it. The Scale-to-Zero documentation states the feature is 'currently in public preview', which is a second reason not to build a 03:00 job on it without a watchdog. The USD 29 hold, the prorated charge and the debit acceptance are all confirmed verbatim on the vendor's pricing FAQ. This is the largest published hold of the seventeen vendors checked, and it is on the free tier.

record.notes: Conflict worth naming: the Free Instance scales to zero after an hour idle, and the TCP Proxy is documented as incompatible with scale-to-zero. A free-tier TCP proxy is therefore expected to work only while something else keeps the service awake.
